extracted.intended_audience: cognitive neuroscientists, psycholinguists, and researchers studying humor using fMRI / experimental paradigms
extracted.subtask_short: fMRI study of verbal humor processing
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, running, and reporting an fMRI experiment that uses three-element verbal jokes to dissociate stages of humor processing (expectation, incongruity, resolution, elaboration). Covers stimulus construction/selection, experimental timing, imaging acquisition/preprocessing, ROI and whole-brain analysis, and behavioral measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-stage model of humor processing
rubrics_metrics.description: The four-stage model comprises the expectation, incongruity, resolution, and elaboration stages of humor processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation = generation of schema/anticipation; Incongruity = detection of semantic conflict/surprise; Resolution = semantic integration and comprehension processes that resolve incongruity; Elaboration = affective/pleasurable responses (amusement). The model extends prior three-stage accounts by adding expectation at the front end to make humor processing more complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mapping joke elements to processing stages (three-element joke design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three-element jokes are structured as setup (expectation), first punch line (incongruity), and second punch line (resolution and elaboration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use three-element jokes to allow within-joke contrasts that directly distinguish expectation, incongruity, resolution, and elaboration processes, reducing inaccuracies inherent in two-element (setup + punch line) designs where the punch line contains multiple processes. Example given: setup → first punch line (incongruity) → second punch line (resolution + elaboration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus selection and staged rating criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the three joke stages (setup, first punch line, second punch line) was rated for funniness, unusualness, and comprehensibility by experts; selection favored specific profiles for each stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure used: 90 three-stage verbal jokes were initially selected and rated by four experts; 60 jokes were chosen such that: setup sentences had low funniness, low unusualness, and high comprehensibility; first punch lines had low funniness, high unusualness, and low comprehensibility; second punch lines had high funniness, low unusualness, and high comprehensibility. Use such staged rating to ensure each element maps reliably onto the intended cognitive stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paired nonjoke baseline construction
rubrics_metrics.description: For each joke, create a paired nonjoke by rewriting first and second punch lines as straightforward, non-incongruous sentences to serve as baseline conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the same setup while removing incongruity/resolution/elaboration from punch lines to create EN, IN, RN baselines that are directly comparable to EJ, IJ, RJ conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental design: 3 × 2 within-subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a 3 (sentence stage: expectation, incongruity, resolution–elaboration) × 2 (type: joke, nonjoke) two-way within-subject design, yielding six conditions (EJ, IJ, RJ, EN, IN, RN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows analysis of main effects and interactions of stage and type; used both interaction and simple main effect analyses to dissociate stage-related activations and type differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral measure: in-scan funniness ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect trial-by-trial funniness ratings during scanning using a 1–4 Likert scale presented after stimuli.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratings presented for 3.5 s, participants indicate 1–4 using different fingers; used as in-scan behavioral dependent variable and analyzed (paired-sample t-test) to confirm jokes elicited higher funniness than nonjokes (example result: mean joke = 2.76 vs nonjoke = 1.46; t(53)=19.04, p<0.001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial timing, run structure, and jittering
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial/run timing conventions used to present three-element sentences and ratings with jittered ISI/ITI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four runs of 15 trials (60 trials total); dummy scan at run start; fixation 500 ms; first sentence 7320 ms, second 5760 ms, third 6750 ms; jittered ISI 700–1200 ms (mean ~1 s); rating 3.5 s; jittered ITI 700–1200 ms (mean ~1 s); 1-minute rest at end of each run. Use similar timings and jitter to separate hemodynamic responses to each sentence element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant inclusion and ethical procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruit healthy volunteers meeting handedness, language, and absence-of-disorder criteria and obtain informed consent and IRB approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 54 healthy volunteers (27 men, 27 women), mean age 24.02, right-handed native Mandarin speakers, no history of mental or neurological disorders; study approved by Research Ethics Committee, informed consent obtained; pre-scan safety checks performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus length constraints (word counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain controlled word counts for each sentence element to keep stimuli comparable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported averages and ranges: setup mean 36.72 words (SD=2.23, range 34–41); first punch line mean 27.16 (SD=2.64, range 22–32); second punch line mean 20.07 (SD=2.61, range 16–25). Nonjoke first and second punch lines had similar ranges. Use comparable length constraints when compiling verbal stimuli.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaging acquisition parameter standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify scanner and sequence parameters appropriate for whole-brain EPI fMRI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example parameters used: 3T Siemens Magnetom Prisma, 20-channel head coil; TR = 2000 ms, TE = 26 ms, flip angle 90°; whole-brain axial acquisition aligned to AC-PC with 40 slices per TR; FOV 220 × 220 cm^2 (as reported), matrix 64 × 64, voxel size 3.4 × 3.4 × 3.4 mm, slice thickness 3.4 mm; dummy scans = 3 TR; up to 210 TRs per run. Report scanner, coil, and visualization hardware (e.g., goggles) and software (E-prime).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprocessing pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform standard preprocessing steps: slice timing, realignment, coregistration, normalization, and smoothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slice timing correction for interleaved acquisition; realignment (six motion parameters) and deletion of runs with excessive or irregular head motion; coregister mean EPI to T1; normalize to MNI template with 3 × 3 × 3 mm voxels; smooth with Gaussian kernel (6 mm FWHM used). Use software such as SPM12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion handling and covariates
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for participant head motion both procedurally and in the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use six head-movement parameters as covariates in GLM to reduce motion artifacts; if head movement is violent/irregular, delete the data and exclude from analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis framework and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Use GLM with canonical HRF for first-level individual analyses and second-level group analyses; apply appropriate multiple-comparison correction and cluster criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: whole-brain voxel-based functional activation analysis with peak-level familywise error (FWE)-corrected p < 0.05; cluster voxels > 10; small volume correction (SVC) applied for some ROIs. Report contrasts of interest (interaction stage × type, simple main effects) and present MNI coordinates and BA where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Region-of-interest (ROI) selection tied to processing stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose ROIs based on prior literature and hypothesized mapping of brain regions to humor processing stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ROIs listed by stage in this study: Incongruity stage ROIs = middle temporal gyrus (MTG) and medial frontal gyrus (MFG); Resolution stage ROIs = inferior frontal gyri (IFG), superior frontal gyrus (SFG), inferior parietal lobule (IPL); Humor/pleasure (elaboration) ROIs = ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC), amygdala, insula, nucleus accumbens (NAc), midbrain. Expectation ROI findings highlighted middle frontal gyrus (MFG) and posterior insula (PI). Use literature-driven ROI definitions and SVC where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast logic to dissociate processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific contrasts to isolate stages—compare elements within three-element jokes (e.g., EJ vs IJ, IJ vs RJ, RJ vs EJ) and compare joke vs nonjoke at each stage (EJ>EN, IJ>IN, RJ>RN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within-material contrasts (expectation vs incongruity vs resolution–elaboration) reduce between-material confounds; comparing joke vs paired nonjoke at each stage isolates humor-specific activations. Interaction analyses (stage × type) can reveal regions sensitive to both stage and humor content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting standards for activations and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Report interaction and simple main effect results with MNI coordinates, BA, side, voxel counts, and corrected statistical values; include figures visualizing stage-specific activations and a model figure mapping stages to neural circuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tables of activations (e.g., Tables 4–6), thresholding details, and illustrative figures for each stage (Expectation, Incongruity, Resolution, Elaboration) and an overall model diagram mapping regions to stages (e.g., Figure 6 in this paper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis framing for three-element materials
rubrics_metrics.description: State explicit hypotheses that (1) materials will replicate effects seen in prior humor fMRI studies, (2) three-element jokes will separate humor processing stages, and (3) adding expectation will expand the framework to a four-stage model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame experimental predictions in relation to prior literature and justify materials/design choices explicitly; use prior ROI findings to form stage-specific predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of practice trials, instructions, and safety procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Include instruction and practice sessions pre-scan, safety checks for MRI, structural scan before functional runs, and debriefing post-scan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide participants with full information (purpose, procedures, rights, MRI safety), run a six-question practice block with identical presentation characteristics to the formal experiment, check for metal objects, and perform T1 anatomical scan prior to functional data acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive linkage between brain regions and psychological processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret activations in canonical regions as reflecting the hypothesized cognitive or affective components of humor processing (e.g., vmPFC correlates with subjective funniness; MTG/MFG with incongruity detection; IFG/SFG/IPL with semantic integration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cautiously relate activations to functions supported by literature (e.g., vmPFC = funniness/valuation; amygdala/NAc/midbrain = reward/pleasure; insula = subjective awareness/interoception). Use contrasts (e.g., joke vs garden-path vs baseline) to support functional claims.
